title: Microinteraction Accessibility Playbook: Sparklines & Chip Clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket is to produce a focused accessibility remediation and evidence playbook for two related microcomponent patterns used across dashboards: (1) inline sparklines (tiny trend graphs rendered as SVG/canvas) and (2) chip clusters / compact action pill groups (micro buttons, filter chips, and indicator badges). These elements are high-density and frequently embedded in tables, list rows, and compact widgets. Current issues reported in QA and by customers include: non-discernible focus outlines at small sizes, missing semantic roles for assistive tech, inadequate keyboard reachability when nested inside virtualized rows, and contrast failures for hover/focus states at tokenized color ramps.

Goals:
- Define a reproducible, component-level remediation plan (design + tokens + dev guidance) that preserves compact density while meeting WCAG 2.1 AA and producing VPAT evidence.
- Provide concrete ARIA role recommendations, keyboard choreography (roving tabindex vs. delegated handlers), and hit-area/touch-target guidance for 32px->24px micro controls.
- Produce test matrices and example test-cases for VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS across Chrome/Firefox/Safari on Mac/Win, and TalkBack on Android for in-app webviews.

Scope & Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc with decision matrix (when to expand hit area, when to surface full label vs abbreviated aria-label).
2) Token mappings: contrast overrides for focus/active states for the compact token set (light/dark/high-contrast).
3) Updated Figma components (sparklines and chip clusters) with annotation layers for a11y states and motion-reduced variants.
4) Example code snippets for: accessible SVG sparklines (role="img" with accessible description; aria-hidden for purely decorative paths), keyboard traversal patterns for nested chips, and pointer-hit-area CSS shim with reduced visual footprint.
5) VPAT evidence checklist and example screenshots/voiceover logs for acceptance.
6) E2E test plan (Cypress + axe-core assertions and voice-level smoke scripts) with sample testcases to be added to design-system repo.

Design trade-offs / notes:
- We will prioritize consistent keyboard behavior for nested clusters over preserving absolute visual compactness; in some table densities we will surface a compact focus affordance and expand on focus (expand-to-overlay pattern) to keep overall layout stable.
- For sparklines, we recommend a single semantic container with accessible summary text rather than adding per-point roles unless the product explicitly needs per-point navigation.
- Avoid adding verbose live regions for frequent real-time updates; use polite live region with debouncing for dashboard refreshes to avoid screen reader noise.

Acceptance criteria: (all must be met for Done)
- Design tokens for focus/hover/active states added to token catalog and validated via Contrast checker for light/dark/high-contrast themes.
- Figma components updated and reviewed by accessibility SME (sign-off from Eng a11y reviewer).
- Example code PR merged into design system repo with: keyboard unit tests, axe-core baseline passing, and documented API for chip cluster keyboard mode toggle (roving vs. linear).
- VPAT checklist completed with at least 3 recorded evidence artifacts (VoiceOver transcript, NVDA screenshot, high-contrast visual).
- Playbook published to Confluence and linked from component README.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Sparklines: use role="img" + aria-labelledby to a visually-hidden summary element that includes min/median/max when configured. Add tabindex=0 to the wrapper for keyboard focus; on focus show a high-contrast focus ring token (token name provided in doc).
- Chips: implement roving-tabindex when chips are actionable and homogenous; for mixed content (icon-only action + dropdown) surface explicit focusable elements and provide aria-haspopup/aria-expanded as appropriate.
- Hit area: apply a 10px invisible padding shim using ::before with pointer-events enabled while keeping visual size.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: compact density requirement from product could push us towards smaller hit targets. Mitigation: canned UX pattern (expand-on-focus overlay) and negotiation with PM to identify critical flows where density cannot be reduced.
- Risk: legacy tables using virtualization may lose focus during re-render. Mitigation: add examples using stable DOM keys and focus-restoration helpers (link to engineering patterns).
